summary: Tested the smart Deep Think auto-router (backend) and jurisdiction pill (frontend, code review only — UI automation was blocked by language modal after 3 loop-prevention attempts). Found and applied one critical fix: the auto-router classifier used a non-existent method `with_max_tokens(4)` on LlmChat, which made the ENTIRE feature silently fail (all complex questions returned deep_think_auto=false via exception fallback). After patching to `.with_params(max_tokens=4)`, all 6 backend tests pass and the router behaves per spec.

critical.issue: LlmChat has no method `with_max_tokens`; only `with_params(max_tokens=…)`. The classifier was raising AttributeError every single call and falling into the except branch that returns False. Net effect: the smart Deep Think auto-router NEVER triggered for any user — the whole feature under review was completely broken as shipped. FIXED IN-PLACE (single line change).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1063 — `.with_max_tokens(4)` is not a real LlmChat method (only with_model, with_params, send_message, etc. are available in emergentintegrations). Bug. Fixed in place.

server.py:1848-1854 — auto-router uses get_quota_remaining peek without race protection. If two auto-triggered requests fire concurrently at quota-1 remaining, both will pass the peek and both will consume, resulting in used=limit+1. Low likelihood but worth noting.

server.py:1043-1069 — the classifier is fire-and-forget on every Pro chat >=60 chars. Adds ~200-400ms latency + tiny Haiku cost per request. Consider adding a lightweight local heuristic (word count, question-mark count, presence of 'my/I/me' + situational verbs) as a pre-filter to skip the LLM call on obviously-simple messages.

server.py streaming endpoint at ~2093-2116 duplicates the auto-router logic verbatim from the non-streaming path — extract to a helper (e.g. maybe_auto_upgrade_deep_think(user, data, tier)) to avoid drift between the two.

Frontend App.js:2685 — the comment says the pill sits 'DIRECTLY UNDER the Lex avatar' but the pill is actually positioned via bottom:-24 relative to the COMPOSER wrapper (padding-bottom:56 leaves room for it). The 'Lex avatar' in scope is the mic button image on the composer bar, not the chat-header avatar. Comment could be clearer.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the auto-router bug: emergentintegrations.llm.chat.LlmChat exposes only these methods: [get_messages, send_message, send_message_multimodal_response, with_model, with_params]. The developer wrote `.with_max_tokens(4)` which was a plausible-looking but non-existent method. Because the entire classifier body is wrapped in try/except with a warning log and returns False on failure, the bug was invisible in tests that only checked HTTP 200 — the request succeeded, deep_think_auto was silently False, and the user got normal Sonnet (not deep-think Sonnet) for every complex question. Detection: only surfaced when I checked backend logs and saw 'WARNING:root:deep-think classifier failed, defaulting to False: AttributeError(\"LlmChat object has no attribute with_max_tokens\")' repeated 3x — one per test call. Mitigation applied: replaced with `.with_params(max_tokens=4)`. Recommend adding a unit test that asserts the classifier does NOT swallow AttributeError, so any future API breaking change surfaces immediately.
